conditions: The graph labels are saved listing addresses. They are not established runtime linear addresses or CPU EIP offsets.

All instruction equations are conditional on default x86 32-bit code/operand/address mode, the captured instruction image applying at each reached label, normal completion, and SS.B=1 for full-ESP stack equations. None of these per-address runtime conditions was queried here.

Let U(x)=x modulo 2^32. A hypothetical mapping lambda(L) sends a listing label to a runtime linear instruction address. With an applicable CS base, rho(L)=U(lambda(L)-CS.base). No lambda or CS base is established. Relative target equalities additionally require lambda to preserve the encoded displacement between the relevant labels; this is required separately for targets outside the owner.

At a CALL with current CPU EIP e and length n, the pushed near return offset is U(e+n). A relative call/jump target is U(e+n+signed_displacement). Only under the mapping/displacement conditions may these be written rho(next_listing_label) or rho(target_listing_label). Numeric listing values require both listing-to-linear identity and CS.base=0, not CS.base=0 alone.

For each designated continuation, the applicable captured code, code mode, mapping and segment/stack conditions must hold again. An opaque callee may change code, registers, flags, memory, segment state or other execution context. A call may fail, diverge, terminate or transfer elsewhere; no exhaustive behavioral classification or return guarantee is inferred.

R(M,seg,o) and W(M,seg,o,v) denote a normally completing little-endian dword read/write using the applicable segment base, limits and memory mapping. Ordered writes update all backing-memory aliases, including partial overlap. The notation neither assumes DS=SS nor assumes distinct linear addresses have distinct backing memory. Memory stability between observations requires a separate environment/volatile/concurrency contract.

restoration_preconditions.register_preservation_precision: The visible body never reads EBP after the initial argument load until POP EBP overwrites it. First/second callee ESI preservation is a sufficient same-offset obligation; an equivalent DS/offset/backing-memory association could suffice instead, and must be established explicitly.
